x: After the half-way mark and turn for home, and two miles of down hill running to go, Brian Hallowell made full use of his long stride to improve his position in the nineties while John Moore and Chas Walker were leading him slightly.

Brian Hallowell produced an encouraging performance in taking us back into the lead once more and David Jones ran consistently in improving the margin to 20 secs; leaving Newell and Dabbs to do no more than underline our superiority.

Brian Hallowell took over on the second stage and appeared to be running smoothly but there was that lack of fire which we have seen from him in earlier runs on the Brighton road and instead of making up some of the lost ground we were dropping even further behind.
Erases two names from the record list--Brian Hallowell and John Davies at 4:10.6. Ranjit now has the honour of being Asia's fastest miler.
When Brian Hallowell set off on the last leg we still had hopes of a higher position than third but the two boys ahead were soon fighting out the lead together and Brian was unable to get to grips.

Brian Hallowell, so long a stalwart of our road-relay teams and no mean miler either (he recorded 4:10.6 in the A.A.A. Championship of 1956) has now bought a house in his native Cheshire and is unlikely to run for us any more.

STAGE 7 - Charlie Dabbs (19:06. 7th) Coming into the team as a result of the illness of John Thresher and an injury to Brian Hallowell, Chas. ran a steady leg across Gatwick Airport but was obviously still feeling the effects of his enforced layoff a few weeks earlier when he underwent a nasal operation.
Brian Hallowell, who was to become John's training partner and rival, placed 2nd. The club records for 880yds. and 1 mile at this time stood to R.T.(Bob) Taylor with 1:53.6 and Jack Brown 4:11.8.
